analysis.investment_thesis: Cohance (formerly Suven Pharmaceuticals) is a CDMO/API business that peaked in FY22 and has been in a multi-year earnings contraction — revenue fell from ₹1,340 Cr (FY23) to ₹1,051 Cr (FY24), and net profit has dropped every year from ₹454 Cr in FY22 to ₹265 Cr in FY25. At an EV/EBITDA of 94.7x on contracting earnings, you are paying a venture-capital multiple for a business going backward.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 57.49% with strong institutional backing (DII 21.57%) provides governance comfort
Gross margin of 71.5% reflects high-value NCE intermediates and oligonucleotide building blocks — premium chemistry
Balance sheet equity jump to ₹3,787 Cr in FY25 (from ₹2,051 Cr) suggests a large inorganic addition that could reshape revenue trajectory
key_risks: Operating income contracting from ₹582 Cr (FY22) to ₹375 Cr (FY25) — a 35% erosion over 3 years with no bottom in sight
Borrowings surged from ₹65 Cr (FY24) to ₹451 Cr (FY25) alongside total asset jump to ₹5,568 Cr — acquisition integration risk is high and unquantified
Operating margin of only 8.89% is dangerously thin for a specialty CDMO; any revenue miss flows straight to PAT
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 94.7x on a business with EBITDA of ₹419 Cr and contracting — this is one of the most expensive valuations in Indian healthcare
Market cap ₹14,955 Cr — Kedia avoids stocks above ₹2,000 Cr; this is 7.5x that ceiling
Net profit declined 4 consecutive years (FY22→FY25): ₹454 → ₹411 → ₹300 → ₹265 Cr — the transformation story is a reversal story, not a growth story
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cohance is paying the price for a business model that was supercharged by a single large NCE customer (likely during a COVID-era CDMO boom) and is now normalizing sharply. The name change from Suven Pharma to Cohance signals strategic repositioning toward oligonucleotides and ADCs, but revenue has yet to show any inflection — the FY25 revenue of ₹1,198 Cr is still 11% below FY22's ₹1,320 Cr peak.

The FY25 balance sheet explosion (total assets +147% to ₹5,568 Cr) suggests a large acquisition has been consummated, but the operating margin collapse to sub-9% and rising borrowings make this a show-me story, not a buy. For Kedia's framework, this fails on size (₹14,955 Cr), valuation (EV/EBITDA 94.7x), earnings trend (4-year contraction), and profitability (ROE 12.7%). Hard avoid.
